title: Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance (ISR) Systems Engineer (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR INTEL
raw_text:
9. MOS 2651, Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance (ISR) Systems Engineer
(GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. ISR Systems Engineers design and implement the integration
and management of ISR platforms, intelligence datasets, and intelligence
networks as members of the signals intelligence and all-source intelligence
production chains. These duties include but are not limited to sensor
integration, ensuring dataflow between intelligence systems, Sensitive
Compartmented Information communications, maintain data standardization,
enterprise support and services, network and data redundancy, and disaster
recovery. Marines assigned this MOS receive training in computer hardware
fundamentals, operating systems, information assurance, database and data
flow management, radio frequency theory, satellite communications,
networking, system integration, network and data science philosophies. This
MOS will be assigned and voided only by the authority of the CMC (MM).
Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC (within their occupational
field) that has been coded with one or more DoD Cyber Workforce Framework
(DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI 8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the
MOS roadmap for additional training and certification requirements associated
with these work role codes.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

        (2) Must possess a CL score of 110 or EL score of 110 or GT score of
100 or higher.

        (3) Must successfully complete a counter-intelligence scope polygraph
examination.

        (4) Security requirement: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background
investigation/T5 investigation.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the Basic SIGINT Operators Course (F07CVT1), San Angelo,
TX.

        (2) Complete the Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance
Engineer Course (F07DZZ1), San Angelo, TX.




                                          3-164                      Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (p), Signals Intelligence Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) Reference the Marine Corps Credentialing Opportunities On-line
(COOL) Program.

            (2) United Services Military Apprenticeship Program (USMAP).

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Intelligence Specialist, 0231.

            (2) Satellite Transmissions System Operator, 0627.

            (3) Network Administrator, 0631.

            (4) Spectrum Manager, 0648.

            (5) COMINT/EW Operator, 2621.

            (6) Surveillance Sensor Operator, 8621.

The Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) OccFld includes the employment of SIGINT, EW, support to cyberspace operations (CO) and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) systems engineering capabilities. Marines in this field are required to set up and operate collection and communications electronic equipment, manage intelligence data, prepare EW and intelligence reports, extend and mesh intelligence services, conduct preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, execute electromagnetic attack (EA), and assist in the operational control and management of SIGINT/EW/CO personnel, equipment, and facilities. Entry- level jobs include Communications Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Operator, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Analyst, Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance Systems Engineer, and Cryptologic Language Analyst. nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
